definition_zh: 上面的；较高的；上部的；上游的；上层的；（地位）较高的
definition_en: higher in position or rank than something else
core_image: 两层抽屉，上面那层要抬手才够得着
scene: 书架从地面一直顶到天花板，最上面那几排书要搬梯子才拿得到。The upper shelves are full of old magazines.
sceneCN: 这里 upper 是「上面的」（第 1 个义项：位置较高的）；句意为上面几层书架塞满了旧杂志。抬手才够得着的上层抽屉，正是这个词的核心。

derivatives.zh: 由 upper 加 -most 构成，义为「最高的；最上面的」
upper 的比较级词尾所由来的原副词，义为「向上」
由 up 加 -wards 构成，义为「向上；朝上」

senses.title: Higher of two parts
senses.definition: higher in position when two parts are compared
senses.definitionCN: 比较两部分时位置较高的那一部分
senses.example: The upper drawer holds the knives.
senses.exampleCN: 上面那层抽屉放的是刀。
senses.why: The word is the old comparative of up, so it simply means the more up of two things.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是 up 较古老的比较级，字面就是「两者中更靠上的那个」。

senses.title: Near the top of a building or body
senses.definition: used of the part of a building or a body nearer the top
senses.definitionCN: 形容建筑或身体靠近顶端的部分
senses.example: He lives on the upper floor of the old house.
senses.exampleCN: 他住在这栋老房子的楼上。
senses.why: A building is vertical, so the part nearer the roof is literally the more up part.
senses.whyCN: 建筑是竖着的，因此靠近屋顶的那部分字面上就是「更靠上的一端」。

senses.title: Higher in rank or class
senses.definition: used of people of higher social or official rank
senses.definitionCN: 形容社会或职务等级较高的人
senses.example: The upper class lived behind the park.
senses.exampleCN: 上层人家住在公园后面。
senses.why: Social rank is pictured as height, and the higher people are said to be in, the more the word applies.
senses.whyCN: 社会等级被画成了高度，人所在的位置越「高」，这个词就用得越贴切。

senses.title: Further up a river
senses.definition: used of the part of a river further from the sea
senses.definitionCN: 形容河流离海较远的一段
senses.example: They swam in the upper reaches of the river.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在河的上游河段游泳。
senses.why: A river runs downhill, so the higher part of the land gives the upper part of the stream.
senses.whyCN: 河往低处流，因此地势较高的那一段就成了溪流的上游。

senses.title: The higher of two limits
senses.definition: used of the highest figure allowed or recorded
senses.definitionCN: 形容允许或记录的最高数值
senses.example: The upper limit for the room is twenty people.
senses.exampleCN: 这个房间的上限是二十人。
senses.why: Two bounds are compared exactly as two shelves are, and the higher one takes the word.
senses.whyCN: 两条界限的比较与两层架子的比较完全一样，较高的那条就用这个词。

senses.title: The top of a shoe
senses.definition: the part of a shoe above the sole
senses.definitionCN: 鞋底以上的部分
senses.example: The uppers are leather, the soles are rubber.
senses.exampleCN: 鞋帮是皮的，鞋底是橡胶的。
senses.why: The part of a shoe that rises above the sole is named by the same word that means the higher of two.
senses.whyCN: 鞋底之上升高起来的那部分，用的仍是表示「较高者」的这个词。

intro.en: The old comparative of up, kept as a separate adjective while the verb moved on.
intro.cn: up 的古老比较级形式，在其他用法继续演变时被保留为独立形容词。

items.en: The root upp means up, and a comparative form existed early in the family.
items.cn: 词根 upp 意为「向上」，这一语族很早就有了比较级形式。

items.en: The word yferra served as the comparative of up and meant higher.
items.cn: 古英语 yferra 充当 up 的比较级，意为「更高的」。

items.en: The form develops into upper, while up remains an adverb and particle.
items.cn: 这一形式后来发展为 upper，而 up 保持副词与小品词的身份。

items.en: Upper takes on social meaning in upper class and upper house.
items.cn: upper 在 upper class、upper house 中获得社会与制度义。

items.en: Concrete uses such as shoe uppers and upper limit keep the word physical.
items.cn: upper 也用于鞋帮、上限这类具体说法，保持着实感。

note.en: The look-alike group collects up- words and their compounds, while the near-meaning group compares words for height and rank.
note.cn: 形近组收集 up 系词及其复合词，近义组比较表示高低与等级的词。

normalIntro.en: One of the few words in English that preserves an old comparative ending outside the usual two-tier pattern.
normalIntro.cn: 英语中少数保留了古老比较级词尾、却不属于通常两级体系的词之一。

normal.en: Upper is the comparison of up, not of a simple adjective.
normal.cn: upper 是 up 的比较形式，并非普通形容词的比较级。

normal.en: The upper hand comes from an old game and now means an advantage.
normal.cn: the upper hand 源自一种古老游戏，现在指占上风。

normal.en: Upper class and upper house are the social and political uses.
normal.cn: upper class 与 upper house 是它的社会与政治用法。

normal.en: Uppermost adds -most for the very top.
normal.cn: uppermost 加 -most 表示最顶端。

normal.en: Shoe uppers are the part above the sole.
normal.cn: shoe uppers 指鞋底以上的那部分。

abstract.en: Reach up for the drawer above your head.
abstract.cn: 伸手去够头顶上方的抽屉。

abstract.en: See two shelves and only the high one is full.
abstract.cn: 看见两层架子，只有上面那层是满的。

abstract.en: Follow a river upstream until the boats stop.
abstract.cn: 顺着河往上游走，直到不见船。

examples.en: The books on the upper shelf are covered with dust.
examples.cn: 上层架子上的书落了灰尘。

examples.en: After two hours she had the upper hand in the argument.
examples.cn: 两小时后，她在争论中占了上风。

examples.en: The town lies on the upper course of the river.
examples.cn: 这个镇位于河流的上游段。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿婆」——阿婆伸手去够柜子最上层那格，够不着就搬来凳子。

root: 古英语 yferra，为 up 的比较级形式，源自日耳曼语词根 upp（向上）；中古英语演变为 upper

sensesIntro.en: One comparison, the more up of two, moves from furniture to buildings, ranks, rivers, limits, and shoes.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个比较「两者中更靠上的」，从家具走到建筑、等级、河流、上限与鞋帮。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand reaching for the higher of two drawers.
core.cn: 核心意象：伸手去够两层抽屉里更上面的那层。

branches.en: The comparison branch: two parts, the higher one.
branches.cn: 比较分支：两部分中较高的那部分。

branches.en: The building branch: floors near the roof.
branches.cn: 建筑分支：靠近屋顶的楼层。

branches.en: The rank branch: people who sit higher in society.
branches.cn: 等级分支：在社会中位置更高的人。

branches.en: The river branch: the part nearer the source.
branches.cn: 河流分支：靠近源头的一段。

branches.en: The limit and shoe branches: a ceiling figure, a shoe top.
branches.cn: 上限与鞋帮分支：封顶的数字、鞋的上部。

intro.en: A comparative form of an old adverb, now working as an adjective in fixed pairs.
intro.cn: 一个古老副词的比较级形式，如今作形容词用于固定搭配。

latinIntro.en: Latin marks higher comparison with the suffix -ior, as in superior and inferus.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语用词尾 -ior 表示较高比较，如 superior 与 inferus。

items.exampleCN: up 加了更古老的比较级词尾。

items.example: The upper limit is ten litres.

definition_zh: 打翻；弄翻；使心烦；使不适；（比赛）意外击败；心烦的；不快的
definition_en: to knock something over, to make someone unhappy, or to beat a stronger opponent unexpectedly
core_image: 手肘一碰，杯子朝桌上倒下去
scene: 婚礼前夜，有人把饮料碰洒在新娘的礼服上，所有人都慌了。The news upset her so much that she could not sleep.
sceneCN: 这里 upset 是「使心烦」（第 2 个义项：让人心里翻腾不快）；句意为这个消息让她心烦得整夜没睡。手肘碰倒杯子的画面，正是这个词的核心。

derivatives.zh: 来自 distress 的过去分词，义为「痛苦的；忧虑的」
由 upset 加 -ing 构成，义为「令人不安的」

senses.title: To knock something over
senses.definition: to make a container or object fall over
senses.definitionCN: 使容器或物体倒下
senses.example: She upset the glass with her elbow.
senses.exampleCN: 她的手肘把杯子碰倒了。
senses.why: The word is up plus set: to set something up, or rather out of its place, until it falls over.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是 up 加 set：把东西从原位「顶起来」，直到翻倒。

senses.title: To make someone unhappy
senses.definition: to make a person worried, hurt, or unhappy
senses.definitionCN: 使人担忧、难受或不快
senses.example: The letter upset him more than he showed.
senses.exampleCN: 那封信让他心烦，比他表现出来的还要厉害。
senses.why: When a mind is knocked off balance like a cup, the person is upset, and the object becomes the feeling.
senses.whyCN: 当心意像杯子一样被弄得失去平衡，人就成了 upset，物象便化为情绪。

senses.title: To disturb a plan or a system
senses.definition: to disturb an arrangement or a process
senses.definitionCN: 扰乱某个安排或进程
senses.example: The storm upset the whole timetable.
senses.exampleCN: 暴风雨打乱了整个时刻表。
senses.why: A plan laid out like objects on a table can be knocked over too, and then nothing stays in place.
senses.whyCN: 摆好的计划就像桌上的物件，也可能被撞翻，之后便没有一样东西待在原位。

senses.title: To beat a stronger opponent
senses.definition: to defeat a team or player expected to win
senses.definitionCN: 击败被判为会赢的一方
senses.example: The visitors upset the champions in the final minute.
senses.exampleCN: 客队在最后一分钟爆冷赢下卫冕冠军。
senses.why: The result turns the table over: the side everyone placed first falls out of its place.
senses.whyCN: 这个结果把牌桌翻了过来：大家早先摆好的那一方从位子上跌落。

senses.title: A disturbed stomach
senses.definition: used of a stomach that feels unsettled
senses.definitionCN: 形容肚子不舒服、翻搅
senses.example: Too much fried food gives him an upset stomach.
senses.exampleCN: 油炸吃得太多，他就肠胃不适。
senses.why: Inside the body the same upsetting happens, and the stomach is described as turned over.
senses.whyCN: 身体内部也发生同样的翻搅，于是肠胃被说成「倒了」。

senses.title: A surprising defeat
senses.definition: a result in which the expected winner loses
senses.definitionCN: 本该获胜的一方却输了的结果
senses.example: The final was a real upset for the home crowd.
senses.exampleCN: 决赛对主场观众来说是个大冷门。
senses.why: The noun keeps the picture of a table turned over, now applied to an expected result.
senses.whyCN: 名词保留了桌面被翻掉的画面，只是这一次用在了原本意料之中的结果上。

intro.en: A two-part compound of native words whose first sense is physical and whose later senses are emotional.
intro.cn: 一个由本土词构成的两部分复合词，最初的意思是身体的，后来的意思是情绪的。

items.en: Up is an old adverb, and settan meant to place or put.
items.cn: up 是古副词，settan 意为「放置」。

items.en: Upsetten means to set up or to overturn, and the two meanings coexist.
items.cn: upsetten 兼有「竖起」与「推翻」两种意思，二者并存。

items.en: The sense of overturning settles first in the physical world of cups and carts.
items.cn: 「打翻」的意思先固定下来，用于杯子和推车这类实物。

items.en: By the eighteenth century upset describes a disturbed mind and a disturbed stomach.
items.cn: 到十八世纪，upset 已用于形容被搅乱的心情与肠胃。

items.en: The sports sense of an unexpected defeat appears in the nineteenth century.
items.cn: 「爆冷」这一体育含义在十九世纪出现。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers up-set compounds and similar forms, while the near-meaning group collects words for troubling someone.
note.cn: 形近组汇集 up 与 set 组成的复合词及相近形式，近义组汇集表示使人难过的词。

entries.definitionCN: 上面（只是拼写相近，词源不同）

entries.definition: the back part of a stage
entries.definitionCN: 舞台后部（只是拼写相近，词源不同）
上升；好转（只是拼写相近，词源不同）

normalIntro.en: A compound image that moves by easy steps from a falling cup to a troubled mind.
normalIntro.cn: 一个复合意象，从翻倒的杯子很自然地过渡到被搅乱的心。

normal.en: Up plus set: set it up so it tips over.
normal.cn: up 加 set：把东西顶起来直到翻倒。

normal.en: Be upset about something is the emotional frame learners need most.
normal.cn: be upset about 是学习者最需要的情绪框架。

normal.en: Upset is irregular: upset, upset, upset.
normal.cn: upset 的三态同形：upset、upset、upset。

normal.en: An upset stomach and a major upset show the two noun senses.
normal.cn: an upset stomach 与 a major upset 展示了两种名词义。

normal.en: Upsetting is the adjective for what causes the feeling.
normal.cn: upsetting 是表示「令人心烦」的形容词。

abstract.en: Nudge a cup with your elbow and watch it tip.
abstract.cn: 用手肘碰一下杯子，看它倒下。

abstract.en: See a chess board pushed an inch off the table.
abstract.cn: 看见棋盘被推离桌沿一点点。

abstract.en: Feel a plan come apart in the space of one phone call.
abstract.cn: 体会一个计划在一通电话里散架。

examples.en: Do not upset the tray when you leave the room.
examples.cn: 出房间时别把托盘碰翻。

examples.en: He was upset for days after the interview.
examples.cn: 面试之后他难受了好几天。

examples.en: The young team upset the favourites in the semi-final.
examples.cn: 这支年轻球队在半决赛爆冷击败了夺冠热门。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿婆塞特」——阿婆塞东西太用力，一下把瓶罐塞翻在地，全家都慌了神。

root: 中古英语 upsetten，由 up（向上）与 setten（放置）复合，原义「竖起、翻覆」，后经「打翻」引申出「打乱、使心烦、爆冷」等义

sensesIntro.en: One tip-over spreads from cups to plans, to a person's mood, to a stomach, to a final score.
sensesIntro.cn: 一次翻倒，从杯子蔓延到计划、人的心情、肠胃，以至终场比分。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a cup knocked over at the table.
core.cn: 核心意象：桌上被碰倒的一只杯子。

branches.en: The object branch: a container goes down on its side.
branches.cn: 物件分支：容器倒向一边。

branches.en: The feeling branch: a mind knocked off its base.
branches.cn: 情绪分支：心意被撞离了底座。

branches.en: The order branch: arrangements turned over.
branches.cn: 秩序分支：安排被翻乱。

branches.en: The contest branch: the expected result is overturned.
branches.cn: 比赛分支：被认定会赢的结局被推翻。

branches.en: The body and score branches: stomach and upset result.
branches.cn: 身体与比分分支：翻搅的肠胃与意外的结果。

intro.en: Two of the commonest English words joined in one verb, with forms that never change.
intro.cn: 两个最常见的英语词合为一个动词，形态从不变化。

latinIntro.en: The Latin verb behind the idea is evertere, to turn out or overturn.
latinIntro.cn: 这一概念背后的拉丁动词是 evertere（翻出、推翻）。

items.example: The setting was a small town.
The cat knocked over the vase.

items.exampleCN: 这是一部让人不安的电影。

definition_zh: 在楼上；到楼上；楼上的
definition_en: on or to a higher floor of a building
core_image: 楼梯尽头透出亮光，人一级级往上走
scene: 老房子一层招待客人，卧室全都放在木楼梯上面那层。The children sleep upstairs and come down for breakfast.
sceneCN: 这里 upstairs 是「在楼上」（第 1 个义项：位于较高的一层）；句意为孩子们睡在楼上，早上下来吃早饭。楼梯尽头透光、人一级级往上走，正是这个词的核心。

derivatives.zh: 把 up 换成 down 构成的反义形式，义为「在楼下」
复合词的后一部分的单数形式，义为「一级台阶」
复合词的前一部分，义为「向上」

senses.title: On a higher floor
senses.definition: situated on the floor above the one being spoken from
senses.definitionCN: 位于说话者所在层的上一层
senses.example: My grandparents live upstairs.
senses.exampleCN: 我祖父母住在楼上。
senses.why: The word is simply up joined to stairs, so it names the place reached by going up a stair.
senses.whyCN: 这个词就是 up 与 stairs 的合体，指的是顺着楼梯往上到达的那一层。

senses.title: Towards a higher floor
senses.definition: used with verbs of movement towards the floor above
senses.definitionCN: 与运动动词连用，表示朝上一层去
senses.example: She carried the tray upstairs.
senses.exampleCN: 她把托盘端到了楼上。
senses.why: Where something rests, movement towards it also goes, so the same word marks both place and direction.
senses.whyCN: 某处既是所在之地，也是移动所向，因此同一个词既可标位置也可标方向。

senses.title: Used before a noun for a room above
senses.definition: used as an adjective before a noun naming a higher room
senses.definitionCN: 作定语放在名词前，指位置较高的房间
senses.example: The upstairs rooms get the morning sun.
senses.exampleCN: 楼上的房间有早上的阳光。
senses.why: Placed before a noun the same word works as an adjective, still pointing to the floor above.
senses.whyCN: 放在名词前，同一个词就起形容词的作用，指向的仍是上面那一层。

senses.title: The upper floor as a place
senses.definition: used as a noun for the floor or part above
senses.definitionCN: 作名词指上面那一层或那一部分
senses.example: The upstairs needs painting this year.
senses.exampleCN: 楼上今年得刷一遍漆。
senses.why: A floor can be spoken of as a thing in itself, and the word then stands alone as a noun.
senses.whyCN: 一层楼也可以被当作一个独立的东西来说，于是这个词就单独作名词。

senses.title: A figure of speech for the mind
senses.definition: used informally of thoughts rather than places
senses.definitionCN: 口语中指「脑子里」而不是实际位置
senses.example: Whatever is going on upstairs, he shows nothing.
senses.exampleCN: 不管他脑子里在想什么，脸上一点也看不出来。
senses.why: Since the head is the top of the body, the floor above is borrowed for what goes on inside it.
senses.whyCN: 头是身体的最上面，因此「上面那层」就被借来说里面发生的事。

intro.en: A plain compound of the old adverb for upward and the noun for the flight of steps.
intro.cn: 一个朴素的复合词，由古老的「向上」副词与表示楼梯的名词合成。

items.en: Staer meant a stair, and up was the old adverb of upward motion.
items.cn: staer 意为「台阶」，up 是表示向上的古副词。

items.en: The plural staires named the whole flight rather than a single step.
items.cn: 复数 staires 指整段楼梯，而非单独一级。

items.en: Compounds of up with place words grow common, as in upstairs and uphill.
items.cn: up 与地点词构成的复合词渐多，如 upstairs、uphill。

items.en: Upstairs works as adverb, adjective, and noun without changing form.
items.cn: upstairs 兼具副词、形容词与名词三种功能，形态不变。

items.en: Downstairs is coined on the same pattern with the opposite adverb.
items.cn: downstairs 以同一模式配上反义副词造出。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers up- and stair-based words, while the near-meaning group collects words of position in a building.
note.cn: 形近组汇集以 up 与 stair 为基础的词，近义组汇集表示楼内位置的说法。

normalIntro.en: Two everyday pieces that need no explanation, and a form that never changes.
normalIntro.cn: 两个无需解释的日常部件，一种从不变化的形态。

normal.en: Up plus stairs: go up the stairs and you are there.
normal.cn: up 加 stairs：上了楼梯就到了。

normal.en: Go upstairs and be upstairs cover motion and position.
normal.cn: go upstairs 与 be upstairs 分别覆盖移动与位置。

normal.en: Before a noun it turns into an adjective with no change.
normal.cn: 放在名词前就成形容词，形态不变。

normal.en: Downstairs is built exactly the same way with the opposite word.
normal.cn: downstairs 用相反的词以完全相同的方式构成。

normal.en: The noun use takes no article in phrases like to the upstairs.
normal.cn: 名词用法在某些短语里不带冠词。

abstract.en: See light at the top of a narrow stair.
abstract.cn: 想象窄楼梯尽头透出的光。

abstract.en: Hear footsteps crossing a ceiling above you.
abstract.cn: 听头顶天花板上走过的脚步声。

abstract.en: Watch a tray carried carefully up a corner.
abstract.cn: 看一只托盘被小心地端过楼梯拐角。

examples.en: The bedrooms are upstairs, and the kitchen is below.
examples.cn: 卧室在楼上，厨房在下面。

examples.en: He ran upstairs to fetch the letter.
examples.cn: 他跑上楼去取那封信。

examples.en: The upstairs flat has been empty since spring.
examples.cn: 楼上那套房子从春天起就空着。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿普斯台尔斯」——阿普踩着每级台阶往上走，一路踩到楼上。

root: 英语复合词：up（向上）+ stairs（楼梯），stairs 源自古英语 staer（台阶）及其复数 staires（整段楼梯）

sensesIntro.en: One higher floor is reached, occupied, named, and finally borrowed for the mind.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一层楼既可抵达、可居住、可指称，最后还被借去形容脑子里。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: light at the top of a stair.
core.cn: 核心意象：楼梯顶端透出的光。

branches.en: The place branch: where someone lives in the house.
branches.cn: 位置分支：人在屋里的落脚处。

branches.en: The direction branch: carrying something up.
branches.cn: 方向分支：把东西端上去。

branches.en: The attributive branch: a room on that floor.
branches.cn: 定语分支：那一层的房间。

branches.en: The noun branch: the part above the ground floor.
branches.cn: 名词分支：一层以上的部分。

branches.en: The figurative branch: what one thinks in secret.
branches.cn: 比喻分支：私下盘算的东西。

intro.en: Two transparent native pieces, with the second one older than it looks.
intro.cn: 两个透明的本土部件，其中后一个比看上去更古老。

latinIntro.en: Latin marks the upper part with the prefix super-, as in superiore parte.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语用前缀 super- 表示上面的部分，如 superiore parte。

items.meaning: a set of stairs in a building

definition_zh: 城市的；都市的；城镇的；具有城市特点的
definition_en: relating to a town or city and to life in it
core_image: 傍晚一片连成线的窗灯
scene: 公交车在高架桥上慢慢挪动，两边楼群一路亮到天边。Air quality in urban areas is a constant concern.
sceneCN: 这里 urban 是「城市的」（第 1 个义项：与城市有关的）；句意为城区的空气质量一直是令人担心的事。连成线的窗灯，正是这个词的核心。

derivatives.zh: 由 urban 加 -ization 构成名词，义为「城市化」
由 urban 加 -ize 构成动词，义为「使城市化」
同源但语义分化，义为「文雅的；有都市风度的」
同源名词，义为「郊区」，sub- 表示「靠近、在下」

senses.title: Belonging to a town or city
senses.definition: connected with a town or city rather than the countryside
senses.definitionCN: 与城镇或城市相关，而非乡村
senses.example: Urban areas grew quickly in the last decade.
senses.exampleCN: 过去十年城区扩展得很快。
senses.why: The adjective comes from the Latin word for city, so its first job is simply to mark what belongs to a city.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词源自拉丁语「城」一词，因此首要功能就是标出「属于城市的」。

senses.title: Characteristic of city living
senses.definition: used of habits, problems, or styles typical of city life
senses.definitionCN: 形容城市生活特有的习惯、问题或风格
senses.example: Noise and crowding are urban problems.
senses.exampleCN: 噪音和拥挤是城市的问题。
senses.why: Once a district exists, the habits that grow in it carry the same adjective.
senses.whyCN: 城区一旦形成，在其中长出来的习惯也就带着同一个形容词。

senses.title: Relating to city government or services
senses.definition: used of the services and authorities of a city
senses.definitionCN: 形容城市的公共服务与市政机构
senses.example: Urban water supply was restored on Monday.
senses.exampleCN: 城区供水星期一恢复了。
senses.why: The adjective marks whatever belongs to a city, and the city's own offices belong to it most directly.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词标出属于城市的事物，而市政府本身最直接地属于它。

senses.title: Designed for dense settlement
senses.definition: used of land used for buildings and roads rather than farming
senses.definitionCN: 形容用于建筑与道路而非耕作的土地
senses.example: Urban land costs far more than farmland.
senses.exampleCN: 城市用地比农田贵得多。
senses.why: The same city picture works on the ground itself: land inside the city is marked out for buildings.
senses.whyCN: 同一幅城市图景落在土地上：城里的地标出来是给房子用的。

senses.title: Polished in manner, in one old sense
senses.definition: an older sense describing refined manners, now kept in the word urbane
senses.definitionCN: 旧义指举止风雅，如今主要见于 urbane 一词
senses.example: His manners were urban in the older sense of the word.
senses.exampleCN: 按这个词的旧义，他的举止相当文雅。
senses.why: City life was once thought to polish people, so the adjective briefly praised good manners as well.
senses.whyCN: 人们一度认为城市生活能使人变得文雅，因此这个形容词也曾用来称赞好举止。

intro.en: A Latin adjective of the city, borrowed straight into English in its original shape.
intro.cn: 一个拉丁语的「城市」形容词，几乎以原形直接借入英语。

items.en: Urbs meant a city, and urbanus meant of a city or belonging to city life.
items.cn: urbs 意为「城市」，urbanus 意为「城市的、都市生活的」。

items.en: Urbanus also came to describe manners thought polished in the city.
items.cn: urbanus 也渐渐用来形容在城里养成的风雅举止。

items.en: The adjective passed through French as urbain before reaching English.
items.cn: 这个形容词经由法语 urbain 再进入英语。

items.en: Urban enters English in the seventeenth century as a plain adjective of the city.
items.cn: urban 于十七世纪进入英语，是朴素的「城市的」形容词。

items.en: Its relatives multiply: urbane for manners, urbanization for a process.
items.cn: 同源词此后增多：urbane 指风度，urbanization 指过程。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words on the Latin city root, while the near-meaning group compares terms of settlement and land.
note.cn: 形近组汇集建在拉丁「城」词根上的词，近义组比较聚落与土地类词。

entries.definition: relating to citizens and a city

normalIntro.en: One Latin root for the city, shared with suburb and urbane.
normalIntro.cn: 一个拉丁语「城」的词根，与 suburb、urbane 同出。

normal.en: Urb- means city: urban, suburb, urbane all contain it.
normal.cn: urb- 意为「城」：urban、suburb、urbane 都含着它。

normal.en: Urban planning and urban areas are the fixed phrases.
normal.cn: urban planning 与 urban areas 是固定搭配。

normal.en: The opposite is rural, not suburban.
normal.cn: 它的反面是 rural，不是 suburban。

normal.en: Urbane looks similar but means polished in manner.
normal.cn: urbane 长得像，意思是「文雅的」。

normal.en: Urbanization names the process, urbanize the verb.
normal.cn: urbanization 指过程，urbanize 是动词。

abstract.en: See a line of windows lit up to the horizon.
abstract.cn: 想象一排窗灯一直亮到天边。

abstract.en: Hear buses and voices under a bridge at night.
abstract.cn: 夜里听桥下的车声与人声。

abstract.en: Look down from a high building at streets in a grid.
abstract.cn: 从高楼俯瞰方格状的街道。

examples.en: Urban life can be exciting but also tiring.
examples.cn: 城市生活令人兴奋，也让人疲惫。

examples.en: The council is reviewing its urban planning rules.
examples.cn: 市议会正在复核城市规划条例。

examples.en: More than half the population now lives in urban areas.
examples.cn: 现在有一半以上的人口住在城区。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「饿本」——到了城里先想的是找个地方填饱肚子，这座城对饿着的人来说就是城市本身。

root: 拉丁语 urbanus（城市的），源自 urbs（城市），经法语 urbain 进入英语；urbs 本指有城墙的城

sensesIntro.en: One root marked the walled city; it now marks districts, problems, services, land use, and once-polished manners.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个原本标出城墙之城的词根，如今标出城区、城市问题、市政、用地与旧日的风雅。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a line of lit windows running to the horizon.
core.cn: 核心意象：一路亮到天边的窗灯。

branches.en: The district branch: the built-up area itself.
branches.cn: 区域分支：建成区本身。

branches.en: The life branch: noise, crowding, speed.
branches.cn: 生活分支：噪音、拥挤与速度。

branches.en: The government branch: city halls and their work.
branches.cn: 市政分支：市政府及其事务。

branches.en: The land branch: plots given to buildings.
branches.cn: 土地分支：划给建筑的地块。

branches.en: The manner branch: the old city ideal of polish.
branches.cn: 风度分支：旧时城里人推崇的风雅。

intro.en: A Latin adjective ending on a root that also gives suburb and urbane.
intro.cn: 一个拉丁形容词词尾压在同时也派生出 suburb 与 urbane 的词根上。

latinIntro.en: Latin urbs, city, with urbicarius for what belongs to a city, and urbanitas for city refinement.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 urbs 指城，urbicarius 指属于城市的，urbanitas 指都市的风雅。

items.example: Suburb means the area near a city.

definition_zh: 催促；力劝；竭力主张；强烈冲动；欲望
definition_en: to try hard to persuade someone to do something, or a strong wish to do it
core_image: 一只手在背后轻轻推着人往前
scene: 医生把复诊单塞进他手里，反复叮咛下个月一定要再来。The doctor urged him to rest for a week.
sceneCN: 这里 urge 是「力劝」（第 1 个义项：反复劝说促使对方去做）；句意为医生力劝他休息一周。背后轻轻推人往前的画面，正是这个词的核心。

derivatives.zh: 由 urge 加 -ncy 构成名词，义为「紧迫；紧急」
同源形容词，义为「紧急的；急迫的」
由 urgent 加 -ly 构成，义为「紧急地」
由 urge 加 -ing 构成名词，义为「敦促；劝告」

senses.title: To press someone to act
senses.definition: to try hard to make someone do something
senses.definitionCN: 努力使某人去做某事
senses.example: She urged him to see a doctor at once.
senses.exampleCN: 她力劝他立刻去看医生。
senses.why: The Latin verb behind it means to press or push, and pressing a person towards an act is its first sense.
senses.whyCN: 其拉丁动词意为「压、推」，把一个人朝某个行动推过去，就是它的第一层意思。

senses.title: To argue strongly for something
senses.definition: to recommend something forcefully in public or in writing
senses.definitionCN: 在公开场合或文章里有力地主张某事
senses.example: The report urges stronger controls on waste.
senses.exampleCN: 报告竭力主张加强废物管控。
senses.why: A push made in words is still a push, and print carries it to many at once.
senses.whyCN: 用言语做出的推仍然是推，而文字能一次推给许多人。

senses.title: A strong wish to act
senses.definition: a strong feeling that one wants to do something
senses.definitionCN: 想做某事的强烈感受
senses.example: He felt a sudden urge to leave the room.
senses.exampleCN: 他突然想离开这个房间。
senses.why: The inner push that makes the urging possible is named by the same word, now as a noun.
senses.whyCN: 促成这种催促的内在推力，用同一个词作名词来表示。

senses.title: A physical need of the body
senses.definition: a need of the body that presses to be satisfied
senses.definitionCN: 身体上必须满足的需求
senses.example: The long ride gave the child an urgent urge to stop.
senses.exampleCN: 长途车让这孩子急着要停车。
senses.why: A body need presses harder than any advice, and the same word covers it.
senses.whyCN: 身体的某种需要比什么劝告都更急着逼人，这个词同样可以指它。

senses.title: Encouragement rather than order
senses.definition: used of support that moves a process on
senses.definitionCN: 形容推动某个进程前行的支持
senses.example: The teacher urged the class towards a harder question.
senses.exampleCN: 老师把全班往更难的问题上领。
senses.why: Pushing need not be harsh; a hand at the back also supports, and the word keeps that softer use.
senses.whyCN: 推并不一定是逼迫，背后那只手也在扶着，这个词保留了这层柔和用法。

senses.title: An impulse one must resist
senses.definition: used of a wish one struggles to control
senses.definitionCN: 形容努力想克制的念头
senses.example: She fought the urge to correct him in public.
senses.exampleCN: 她克制住了当场纠正他的念头。
senses.why: When the push comes from inside and no one asked for it, the impulse is something to be resisted.
senses.whyCN: 当推力来自内部、并非别人要求时，这股冲动就成了需要忍住的东西。

intro.en: A Latin verb of pressing that arrives through French with its pressure intact.
intro.cn: 一个表示「压」的拉丁动词，带着那股压力经法语进入英语。

items.en: Urgere meant to push, press, or drive on.
items.cn: urgere 意为「推、压、驱赶」。

items.en: The noun urging meant a pressure or a compelling need.
items.cn: 其名词形式指压力或强烈的要求。

items.en: The verb came into French and carried the sense of pressing someone.
items.cn: 这个动词进入法语，带着「催逼某人」的意思。

items.en: Urge enters English and takes the frame urge someone to do.
items.cn: urge 进入英语后形成 urge someone to do 的框架。

items.en: The noun sense of a strong impulse develops later and becomes very common.
items.cn: 名词「强烈冲动」的意思后来发展起来，用法非常普遍。

items.en: Urgent and urgency keep the older idea of pressing need.
items.cn: urgent 与 urgency 则保留了「急迫需要」这一更古老的观念。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the urg- root, while the near-meaning group collects verbs of persuading and pressing.
note.cn: 形近组沿 urg- 词根展开，近义组汇集表示劝说与催促的动词。

normalIntro.en: One root of pushing supplies the verb, the noun, and the whole urgent family.
normalIntro.cn: 一个表示「推」的词根供出动词、名词和整个 urgent 词族。

normal.en: Urge somebody to do is the frame to learn first.
normal.cn: urge somebody to do 是最先要记的框架。

normal.en: The noun takes an article: a sudden urge, the urge to run.
normal.cn: 名词要带冠词：a sudden urge、the urge to run。

normal.en: Urge on means to encourage, urge against means to warn.
normal.cn: urge on 意为鼓励，urge against 意为力劝不要。

normal.en: Urgent and urgency share the same pressing root.
normal.cn: urgent 与 urgency 共享同一个「压」的词根。

normal.en: Feel an urge is internal; urge someone is external.
normal.cn: feel an urge 是内部的，urge someone 是外部的。

abstract.en: Feel a hand at your back pushing gently forward.
abstract.cn: 体会一只手在背后轻轻往前推。

abstract.en: See a door held open by someone insistent.
abstract.cn: 看见有人执意替你把门扶着。

abstract.en: Notice a foot tapping before a decision is made.
abstract.cn: 注意在做出决定之前一直在点的脚。

examples.en: Friends urged her to apply for the scholarship.
examples.cn: 朋友们力劝她去申请那笔奖学金。

examples.en: He resisted the urge to check his phone again.
examples.cn: 他忍住没有再看一次手机。

examples.en: The report urged that the rules be changed at once.
examples.cn: 报告竭力主张立即修改这些规定。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「饿急」——饿急了的人一直催着上菜，那股急切劲儿就是 urge。

root: 拉丁语 urgere（推、压、驱赶），经法语进入英语；urgent、urgency 同出此根

sensesIntro.en: One pressure from behind becomes persuasion, then public argument, then an inner impulse that presses just as hard.
sensesIntro.cn: 一份来自背后的压力先成劝说，再成公开主张，最后成同样逼人的内在冲动。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand at the back pushing forward.
core.cn: 核心意象：背后那只往前推的手。

branches.en: The persuasion branch: one person pressing another.
branches.cn: 劝说分支：一个人压着另一个人。

branches.en: The public branch: a report pressing a case.
branches.cn: 公开分支：报告在力推一个主张。

branches.en: The impulse branch: the same push, now inside.
branches.cn: 冲动分支：同一个推力，转到内部。

branches.en: The body branch: a need that will not wait.
branches.cn: 身体分支：等不得的需求。

branches.en: The support and restraint branches: moving a process, holding back a wish.
branches.cn: 支持与克制分支：推动进程、忍住念头。

intro.en: A Latin root of pushing that gives a verb, a noun, and a large adjective family.
intro.cn: 一个表示「推」的拉丁词根，派生出一个动词、一个名词和一大串形容词。

latinIntro.en: Latin urgere, with its participle urgens and noun urgentia, sits behind the whole family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 urgere 连同分词 urgens、名词 urgentia 是整族词的底子。

items.example: He felt the urgency of the task.
items.exampleCN: 他感到这项任务很紧迫。

definition_zh: 紧急的；急迫的；迫切的；亟待处理的
definition_en: needing immediate attention or action
core_image: 一封信被封上红色加急标签，快递员一路按着喇叭冲进院子
scene: 深夜办公室的灯还亮着，桌上摊着一份标红的文件，秘书站在门口不知该不该打断会议。The doctor received an urgent call and left at once.
sceneCN: 这里 urgent 是「紧急的」（第 1 个义项：需要立刻处理）；句意为医生接到一个紧急电话，立刻离开了。红色加急标签催促着人马上动手，就是这个词的样子。

pos.zh: 形容词：紧急的、急迫的；迫切的；催得很急的

derivatives.zh: 名词，义为「紧迫、紧急」，加 -cy 构成
加 -ly 构成，义为「紧急地、迫切地」
动词，义为「催促、力劝」，是 urgent 的同源动词
名词，义为「催促、劝告」，是 urge 的动名词

senses.title: Needing quick action
senses.titleCN: 急需处理：必须马上动手
senses.definition: requiring immediate attention or action
senses.definitionCN: 需要立刻关注或采取行动
senses.example: The doctor received an urgent call and left at once.
senses.exampleCN: 医生接到一个紧急电话，立刻离开了。
senses.why: Latin urgere means to press or push; something urgent presses on you until you move.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 urgere 意为「压、推」；紧急之事就是这样一直压着你，直到你动起来。

senses.title: Sounding insistent
senses.titleCN: 催促的语气：说得急而不容拖延
senses.definition: expressed with insistence, asking someone to act at once
senses.definitionCN: 带着不容拖延的语气，要求别人立即行事
senses.example: Her letter was an urgent plea for help.
senses.exampleCN: 她的信是一封急切的求助呼吁。
senses.why: The pressure of the verb passes into the voice: the words themselves push the reader.
senses.whyCN: 动词的压迫感进入声音：字句本身在推着读者走。

senses.title: A pressing need
senses.definition: a strong and immediate need for something
senses.definitionCN: 对某物强烈而即时的需求
senses.example: The village is in urgent need of clean water.
senses.exampleCN: 这个村庄急需干净的水。
senses.why: A need that presses is one that cannot wait for next month.
senses.whyCN: 会「压迫」的需求，就是等不到下个月的那种需求。

senses.title: Important and pressing
senses.titleCN: 重要而急迫：事情本身分量重
senses.definition: important enough that delay would cause harm
senses.definitionCN: 重要到一旦拖延就会造成损害
senses.example: Finding shelter became urgent as the storm grew.
senses.exampleCN: 随着暴风雨加剧，找到避难所变得紧迫起来。
senses.why: Urgency here is not noise but weight: the matter presses because the cost of delay is high.
senses.whyCN: 这里的紧迫不是喧闹而是分量：拖延代价高，事情才压得紧。

intro.en: Urgent comes from the Latin verb urgere, to press or drive on, through its present participle urgens.
intro.cn: urgent 来自拉丁语动词 urgere「压、驱赶」，取其现在分词 urgens。

items.en: The verb urgere meant to push, press or drive something forward.
items.cn: 动词 urgere 意为推、压、把某物向前赶。

items.en: Its present participle urgens described whatever is pressing at this very moment.
items.cn: 它的现在分词 urgens 描述此刻正在施压的东西。

items.en: Old French took the participle as urgent, still carrying the pressure of the Latin verb.
items.cn: 古法语把这一分词借作 urgent，仍带着拉丁动词的压迫感。

items.en: English borrowed urgent in the fifteenth century for matters that would not wait.
items.cn: 英语在十五世纪借入 urgent，用来指不容等待的事情。

items.en: Modern usage pairs it with need, action and care, all situations where delay costs something.
items.cn: 现代用法把它和 need、action、care 搭配，都是拖延会付出代价的情形。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the urg- stem and its Latin family; the near-meaning group holds synonyms about haste and necessity.
note.cn: 形近组沿 urg- 词干及其拉丁词族；近义组收表示急切与必要的近义词。

entries.definition: To press someone to act; the verb behind urgent.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「催促、力劝」，是 urgent 背后的动词。

entries.definition: The quality of being urgent; the noun built on it.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「紧迫性」，由 urgent 构成。

entries.definition: In an urgent manner; the adverb.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「紧急地」，是它的副词形式。

entries.definition: Medical help for problems that cannot wait.
entries.definitionCN: 名词短语，义为「急诊服务」，指不能等待的医疗。

entries.definition: Needing action now; literally weighing on you.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「紧迫的」，字面上就是压在你身上。

entries.definition: Absolutely necessary; stronger and more formal.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「必须的」，更正式也更绝对。

entries.definition: So important that failure would be serious.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「关键的、危急的」，失败后果严重。

entries.definition: Happening without delay, without the sense of pressure.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「立即的」，但不含压力感。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the pressing image of the Latin verb and real collocations such as urgent need.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子使用拉丁动词的「压」意象，以及 urgent need 这类真实搭配。

normal.en: Urgent shares a root with urge: both push somebody to move.
normal.cn: urgent 与 urge 同根，都在推动某人行动。

normal.en: An urgent call is one you answer before you finish your tea.
normal.cn: 紧急电话就是茶没喝完就得接的那种电话。

normal.en: In urgent need means the need is pressing right now.
normal.cn: in urgent need 指此刻就急得压人。

normal.en: Urgent care is the clinic you go to when waiting is not an option.
normal.cn: urgent care 就是不能等时去的那种诊所。

normal.en: Mark urgent on an envelope and the postman hurries.
normal.cn: 在信封上写 urgent，邮差就会加快脚步。

abstract.en: The whole word is a hand on your back: urgency is pressure whose source you may not even see.
abstract.cn: 整个词就是一只推着你后背的手：紧迫感来自一种你甚至看不见的压力。

abstract.en: Something is urgent when the cost of waiting exceeds the cost of acting.
abstract.cn: 一件事之所以紧急，是因为等待的代价超过了行动的代价。

abstract.en: Urgency is a comparison in time, not a size: the small thing that must be done now outranks the big thing that can wait.
abstract.cn: 紧迫是时间上的比较而非体量：必须现在做的小事，压过可以等的大事。

examples.en: There is an urgent need for more nurses in the region.
examples.cn: 该地区急需更多护士。

examples.en: He sent an urgent message asking us to postpone the meeting.
examples.cn: 他发来紧急消息，要求我们推迟会议。

examples.en: The repairs are urgent because the roof leaks badly.
examples.cn: 修理很紧急，因为屋顶漏得很厉害。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「饿真急」——饿了真急，得马上找饭吃：紧急的

root: 源自拉丁语动词 urgere「压、驱赶」的现在分词 urgens，经古法语 urgent 于十五世纪进入英语；同族词有 urge、urgency、urgently。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses of urgent move from the call that must be answered to the need, the plea and the weight of the matter.
sensesIntro.cn: urgent 的四个义项从必须接的电话，走到需求、诉求与事情本身的分量。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a red label on an envelope, and a hand pushing you towards the door.
core.cn: 核心意象：信封上的红色标签，以及一只把你推向门口的手。

branches.en: TIME LINE: the thing must be done at once.
branches.cn: 时间线：这件事必须立刻完成。

branches.en: VOICE LINE: the words themselves push the reader.
branches.cn: 声音线：字句本身在推动读者。

branches.en: NEED LINE: what is missing is missing badly.
branches.cn: 需求线：缺的东西缺得很厉害。

branches.en: WEIGHT LINE: delay would cause real harm.
branches.cn: 分量线：拖延会造成真实损害。

branches.en: CONTRAST: important can wait, urgent cannot.
branches.cn: 对照线：重要的可以等，紧急的不能等。

intro.en: Urgent is a Latin participle stripped of its ending and used as an English adjective.
intro.cn: urgent 是一个去掉词尾的拉丁分词，直接充当英语形容词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin pieces are clear: the verb urgere and the participle ending -ens, -entis.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁构件很清楚：动词 urgere 与分词词尾 -ens、-entis。

items.example: It is the root of urgent.
It turns the verb into an adjective.
It forms insurgent from the same verb.
items.exampleCN: 它和同一动词构成 insurgent。

items.example: It forms surge from the same verb.
items.exampleCN: 它和同一动词构成 surge。

items.example: It shows the word in a fixed phrase.
items.exampleCN: 它展示了这个词的固定搭配。

definition_zh: 我们（宾格）；我们（口语里作表语）；咱们
definition_en: the speaker together with other people, used as the object form of we
core_image: 一圈人彼此搭着肩膀，手往自己身上和身边同伴指过去
scene: 老师站在讲台上环视全班，用手指着自己的胸口又划向所有学生。Please wait for us outside the gate.
sceneCN: 这里 us 是「我们（宾格）」（第 1 个义项：动作的接受者）；句意为请在门口等我们。手指从自己划向同伴的动作，就是这个词的样子。

derivatives.zh: 代词，义为「我们」的主格形式
限定词，义为「我们的」，用在名词前
代词，义为「我们的（东西）」，独立使用
代词，义为「我们自己」，反身形式
古旧说法，义为「朝向我们这边」，现已罕用

senses.title: The object form
senses.titleCN: 宾格我们：动作落到我们身上
senses.definition: the object form of we, used after a verb or a preposition
senses.definitionCN: we 的宾格形式，用在动词或介词之后
senses.example: Please wait for us outside the gate.
senses.exampleCN: 请在门口等我们。
senses.why: English keeps a separate shape for we as a target; us is that shape, worn down by centuries of speech.
senses.whyCN: 英语为作为「接受者」的 we 保留了另一个形状，us 就是这个形状，被数百年的口语磨损得极短。

senses.title: The speaker and others
senses.definition: the speaker together with one or more other people, excluding the listener
senses.definitionCN: 说话人和一个或多个其他人，不含听话人
senses.example: They invited us but not our neighbours.
senses.exampleCN: 他们邀请了我们，却没邀请我们的邻居。
senses.why: The group is drawn around the speaker alone; the listener stands outside the circle.
senses.whyCN: 这个圈子只围着说话人画，听话人站在圈外。

senses.title: Including the listener
senses.definition: a warm or informal use that draws the listener into the group
senses.definitionCN: 一种亲切或口语的用法，把听话人拉进群里
senses.example: Come on, let us give it one more try.
senses.exampleCN: 来吧，咱们再试一次。
senses.why: Add the listener and we becomes us in a friendly sense, the tone of a shared task.
senses.whyCN: 把听话人加进来，we 就成了亲切的 us，共用一件事的口吻。

senses.title: After a preposition
senses.definition: the form required after most prepositions such as with, for or to
senses.definitionCN: 跟在 with、for、to 等多数介词后必须使用的形式
senses.example: There is no need to worry about us.
senses.exampleCN: 没有必要为我们担心。
senses.why: Grammar fixes the shape here: prepositions never take the subject form we.
senses.whyCN: 语法在这里锁定了形状：介词后从不接主格 we。

senses.title: In informal agreement
senses.titleCN: 口语句尾：跟着附和一句「我们也是」
senses.definition: a short reply in speech, meaning the same is true of us
senses.definitionCN: 口语里的简短回答，意为「我们也一样」
senses.example: They are coming, and so are we, all of us.
senses.exampleCN: 他们要来，我们也来，我们全体都来。
senses.why: The tiny word does a lot of social work: it turns a statement about them into one about us.
senses.whyCN: 这个小词承担了社交工作：把关于他们的陈述变成关于我们。

intro.en: Us is the worn-down object form of the old Germanic pronoun we, sharing a root with German uns and Dutch ons.
intro.cn: us 是古老的日耳曼语代词 we 被磨短的宾格形式，与德语 uns、荷兰语 ons 同源。

items.en: Old English used us beside the dative form usic, both meaning we as an object.
items.cn: 古英语用 us 表示宾格，另有与格 form usic，意思都是作为宾语的我们。

items.en: The Germanic form uns appears in German as uns and in Dutch as ons, unchanged in sense.
items.cn: 日耳曼形式 uns 见于德语 uns 与荷兰语 ons，意义不变。

items.en: Middle English lost the dative ending, leaving us to cover both object roles.
items.cn: 中古英语丢掉了与格词尾，us 于是同时承担两种宾语角色。

items.en: The final s softened to a voiced sound in unstressed speech, though the strong form kept it sharp.
items.cn: 在非重读语流里末尾的 s 变成浊音，而重读形式仍然保持清音。

items.en: Fixed phrases such as let us and all of us froze the word in daily use.
items.cn: let us、all of us 等固定搭配把这个词冻在日常生活里。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the pronoun family; the near-meaning group gathers other pronouns of person and group.
note.cn: 形近组收同一代词族；近义组收其他表示人称与群体的代词。

entries.definition: The subject form of the same pronoun.
entries.definitionCN: 代词，义为「我们」，同族代词的主格。

entries.definition: The possessive form used before a noun.
entries.definitionCN: 限定词，义为「我们的」，名词前的所有格。
代词，义为「我们的（东西）」，独立使用。

entries.definition: The reflexive form for a plural we.
entries.definitionCN: 代词，义为「我们自己」，复数的反身形式。

entries.definition: The same object role, but only for the speaker.
entries.definitionCN: 代词，义为「我（宾格）」，只指说话人一人。

entries.definition: The person or people spoken to, not spoken of.
entries.definitionCN: 代词，义为「你、你们」，指听话人。

entries.definition: Other people as the object, outside both circles.
entries.definitionCN: 代词，义为「他们（宾格）」，画外的一方。

entries.definition: All people, including speaker and listener.
entries.definitionCN: 代词，义为「每个人」，包括说话人与听话人。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the pronoun family and the real phrases us often appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子使用代词一族与该词真实出现的搭配。

normal.en: We does the action, us receives it: They called us.
normal.cn: we 做动作，us 承受动作：打电话的是他们，被呼叫的是我们。

normal.en: Let us in speech often becomes let’s, with the us folded away.
normal.cn: 口语里 let us 常缩成 let’s，us 被折没了。

normal.en: All of us is a crowd, one of us is a single member.
normal.cn: all of us 是一群人，one of us 其中一员。

normal.en: Us is two letters but the shortest word for company.
normal.cn: us 只有两个字母，却是一个表示同伙的最短的词。

normal.en: After a preposition, English insists on us, never we.
normal.cn: 介词之后英语只认 us，从不写 we。

abstract.en: Us is a boundary word: it marks where the speaker’s circle ends and everyone else begins.
abstract.cn: us 是一个边界词：它标出说话人的圈子到哪儿结束、别人从哪儿开始。

abstract.en: The word shrinks as the group grows: the more people it covers, the shorter the sound.
abstract.cn: 这个词越短反而覆盖的人越多：越被磨小的声音，指的人越广。

abstract.en: Every use of us is a small act of alliance, deciding who stands inside.
abstract.cn: 每一次说 us 都是一次小小的结盟，决定谁站在圈内。

examples.en: Please wait for us outside the gate.
examples.cn: 请在门口等我们。

examples.en: They invited us to dinner on Saturday.
examples.cn: 他们邀我们周六去吃晚饭。

examples.en: Most of us had never seen snow before.
examples.cn: 我们大多数人以前从没见过雪。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「啊死」——啊，死也要一起去：我们

root: 源自古英语代词 us（宾格/与格），与德语 uns、荷兰语 ons 同属日耳曼语形式 uns；同族词有 we、our、ours、ourselves。

sensesIntro.en: Us covers the plain object form, the circle around the speaker, the friendly inclusion and a few fixed grammar slots.
sensesIntro.cn: us 覆盖了普通宾格、说话人的圈子、亲切的包容，以及几个固定语法位置。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a circle drawn around the speaker and some companions, with the listener possibly inside.
core.cn: 核心意象：以说话人为中心画一个圈，圈里是若干同伴，听话人可能在圈内也可能在圈外。

branches.en: GRAMMAR LINE: the form used after verbs and prepositions.
branches.cn: 语法线：动词和介词之后使用的形式。

branches.en: BOUNDARY LINE: the speaker plus others, not the listener.
branches.cn: 边界线：说话人加若干他人，不含听话人。

branches.en: WARMTH LINE: the listener is drawn inside the circle.
branches.cn: 亲切线：听话人被拉进圈内。

branches.en: SOCIAL LINE: a short reply that agrees for the whole group.
branches.cn: 社交线：为整组人表示同意的简短回答。

branches.en: CONTRAST: we acts, us is acted upon.
branches.cn: 对照线：we 发动作，us 受动作。

intro.en: Us has no affixes; it is a single pronoun stem inherited whole from Old English.
intro.cn: us 没有词缀，是从古英语整块继承下来的代词词干。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin in this word; the pronoun is Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词里没有拉丁成分，整个代词属于日耳曼语。

items.example: It is the subject partner of us.
items.exampleCN: 它是 us 的主格搭档。

items.example: It forms himself and herself too.
items.exampleCN: 它也构成 himself 与 herself。

definition_zh: 使用；利用；消耗；用掉；对待
definition_en: to do something with a tool or thing for a purpose, or to take and consume something
core_image: 伸手把工具从抽屉里拿出来握在手中
scene: 厨房的抽屉一拉开，里面躺着各式各样的工具，母亲总能顺手拿出合适的那个。A good cook knows how to use every pot in the kitchen.
sceneCN: 这里 use 是「使用、利用」（第 1 个义项：拿工具去做事）；句意为好厨师懂得使用厨房里的每一口锅。伸手取工具的这幅画面，正是这个词的核心。

derivatives.zh: 动词加 -er 构成，义为「用户；使用者」
加名词后缀 -age 构成，义为「用法；使用量」
加 -ful 构成，义为「有用的」
加 -less 构成，义为「无用的」
加 -able 构成，义为「可用的」

senses.title: To employ a thing for a purpose
senses.definition: to do something with a tool, object, or method in order to achieve a result
senses.definitionCN: 为了达到某个结果而用工具、物品或方法去做事
senses.example: She used a sharp knife to cut the bread.
senses.exampleCN: 她用一把快刀切面包。
senses.why: The verb names the act of taking something into one's hands and making it serve a purpose.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初就指「把东西拿到手里，让它为自己办事」，取用工具的意象就是它的本义。

senses.title: To spend or consume a supply
senses.definition: to consume an amount of something such as time, money, or fuel
senses.definitionCN: 消耗掉一定量的时间、金钱或燃料等
senses.example: The old truck uses a lot of fuel.
senses.exampleCN: 这辆旧卡车很费油。
senses.why: Whatever is put to work is partly spent in the process, so the same verb comes to mean using up a supply.
senses.whyCN: 东西一旦被动用来干活，过程中总要耗掉一部分，于是同一个动词就引申为「耗用」。

senses.title: The act or purpose of employing something
senses.definition: as a noun, the act of employing something or the purpose it serves
senses.definitionCN: 作名词时指使用的行为，或某物所起的作用
senses.example: This room is for the use of guests only.
senses.exampleCN: 这个房间仅供客人使用。
senses.why: The nouns formed from the verb simply name the action itself and the end it serves.
senses.whyCN: 由这个动词转成的名词只是把「使用」这个动作本身和它所服务的目的命名下来。

senses.title: To treat someone in a particular way
senses.definition: to behave towards somebody in a stated manner, often unfairly
senses.definitionCN: 以某种方式对待某人，常含有不公平的意味
senses.example: He felt that his boss had used him badly.
senses.exampleCN: 他觉得老板待他很刻薄。
senses.why: To use people is to treat them as tools; from that picture the verb widens into simply meaning to treat.
senses.whyCN: 把人当工具使，就是把对方当成器物；从这个画面出发，词义又扩大到泛指的「对待」。

senses.title: To take a drug or apply a substance
senses.definition: to take a drug, medicine, or other substance regularly or deliberately
senses.definitionCN: 有意识地、经常地服用药物或使用某种物质
senses.example: The doctor told him to use the cream twice a day.
senses.exampleCN: 医生让他每天涂两次这种药膏。
senses.why: Medicine is a supply applied to the body for a result, so it slips naturally into the same frame.
senses.whyCN: 药物就是施用于身体、换取疗效的东西，于是它自然套进了同一个句法框架。

intro.en: A short word from Old French, ultimately from Latin, that has kept its shape almost unchanged for eight centuries.
intro.cn: 一个来自古法语、最终可溯至拉丁语的小词，八百年来词形几乎没有变化。

items.en: Usus, the past participle of uti, meant a using or a practice, and usare was a frequentative form of the same verb.
items.cn: usus 是 uti 的过去分词，意为「使用、惯行」；usare 是同一动词的反复体形式。

items.en: Us, user, and the past participle usé carried the verb into everyday French for using and wearing out.
items.cn: us、user 以及过去分词 usé 把这个动词带进日常法语，兼表「使用」与「用旧」。

items.en: English borrows the verb in the thirteenth century as usen, with the noun use beside it.
items.cn: 英语在十三世纪以 usen 的形式借入这个动词，名词 use 并行存在。

items.en: Spelling settles on use, and the word already covers tools, supplies, and medicine.
items.cn: 拼写固定为 use，词义这时已覆盖工具、物资与药物。

items.en: The question what is this used for turns the verb and noun into the commonest way of asking about purpose.
items.cn: what is this used for 这类问句让动词和名词成为询问用途最常用的手段。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the close relatives of the verb, while the near-meaning group sets tools against overuse and waste.
note.cn: 形近组收集这个动词的近亲，近义组则把使用与误用、滥用、浪费放在一起对照。

entries.definition: the way a word or thing is used
to use a tool or method
to use something badly or cruelly
to spend without any useful result

normalIntro.en: Three letters that name the everyday act of taking a thing and making it work for you.
normalIntro.cn: 三个字母，命名的是日常里把东西拿来替你办事的动作。

normal.en: Use up means finish the supply, as in use up all the paper.
normal.cn: use up 表示把存货用尽，如 use up all the paper。

normal.en: Make use of is the fixed phrase for turning something to your advantage.
normal.cn: make use of 是「加以利用」的固定说法。

normal.en: In use describes a machine that is working at this moment.
normal.cn: in use 形容机器此刻正在使用中。

normal.en: The noun use is pronounced with a soft s, the verb with a hard z.
normal.cn: 名词 use 末尾读清音 s，动词则读浊音 z。

normal.en: User, usage, useful, and useless all sit on this same short base.
normal.cn: user、usage、useful、useless 都建立在这个短词干上。

abstract.en: Picture a drawer of knives and spoons, and a hand closing on exactly the right one.
abstract.cn: 想象一抽屉的刀叉勺子，一只手正好抓住了对的那一件。

abstract.en: Feel the grip of a handle that many other hands have worn smooth.
abstract.cn: 体会一只被许多只手磨得光滑的把手。

abstract.en: Watch a full jar of coffee slowly empty day after day.
abstract.cn: 看着满满一罐咖啡一天天空下去。

examples.en: She used an old spoon to dig a hole for the seeds.
examples.cn: 她用一把旧勺子挖了个坑埋种子。

examples.en: We used up all the firewood before the snow came.
examples.cn: 雪落下之前我们把木柴都用光了。

examples.en: Learning to use a map is still a useful skill on long hikes.
examples.cn: 学会用地图在长途徒步中仍是一项有用的技能。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「优使」——把最好用的工具交给能干的人去使用。

root: 拉丁语 uti（使用）及其过去分词 usus、反复体 usare，经古法语 us / user 进入英语

sensesIntro.en: One act of taking a thing into service spreads to spending supplies, to the act itself, to treating people, and to taking medicine.
sensesIntro.cn: 从「把东西拿来用」这一个动作出发，词义扩展到耗用物资、使用行为、对待他人以及服用药物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand taking a tool and putting it to work.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手取出工具，让它开始干活。

branches.en: The tool branch: a thing made to serve a purpose.
branches.cn: 工具分支：让某物为某个目的服务。

branches.en: The supply branch: use eats into a store of fuel, money, or time.
branches.cn: 物资分支：使用会吃掉油、钱、时间的存量。

branches.en: The noun branch: the act itself and the purpose it serves.
branches.cn: 名词分支：使用这一行为以及它服务的目的。

branches.en: The people branch: treating someone as a tool.
branches.cn: 人事分支：把某人当作工具来对待。

branches.en: The medicine branch: a substance applied for a result.
branches.cn: 药物分支：为求疗效而施用的物质。

intro.en: The word is barely analysable today, but two Latin pieces are still readable behind it.
intro.cn: 这个词如今几乎无法拆分，但其背后仍能读出两个拉丁成分。

latinIntro.en: The Latin verb uti, to use, gives usus and the frequentative usare; the short stem is all that survives in English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁动词 uti（使用）给出 usus 与反复体 usare，英语只留下了这条短词干。

items.example: The stem us- carries the whole idea of using.
items.exampleCN: 词干 us- 承载了「使用」的全部含义。

items.example: Use as a verb keeps a silent final e.
items.exampleCN: 作动词的 use 末尾有一个不发音的 e。

items.example: Use gives user, a person who uses.
items.exampleCN: use 加它成为 user，即使用者。

items.example: Usage means the way or amount of use.
items.exampleCN: usage 表示用法或使用量。

items.example: Usable means able to be used.
Misuse is the wrong kind of use.

definition_zh: 有用的；有益的；实用的
definition_en: helpful for doing something, or able to serve a practical purpose
core_image: 一把随身小刀，开箱、削果、割绳样样都行
scene: 出门前母亲往包里塞了一把折刀，说路上总会有用得着的时候。A small torch is really useful when the power fails.
sceneCN: 这里 useful 是「有用的」（第 1 个义项：能派上用场）；句意为停电时手电筒真的很有用。随身小刀件件都能用的画面，正是这个词的核心。

derivatives.zh: 加 -ly 构成副词，义为「有用地；有益地」
加 -ness 构成名词，义为「有用性；实用性」
去掉后缀后的基础词，义为「使用」
换成否定后缀 -less，义为「无用的」

senses.title: Helpful for a practical purpose
senses.definition: able to help someone do something or reach a result
senses.definitionCN: 能够帮助某人做成某件事或达到某个结果
senses.example: Her advice was useful, and I changed my plan.
senses.exampleCN: 她的建议很有用，我因此改了计划。
senses.why: The base verb names putting a thing to work; the suffix means full of, so the adjective marks what is full of workable use.
senses.whyCN: 基础动词指「让东西干活」，后缀意为「充满」；所以这个词就是「充满可用之处」的东西。

senses.title: Worth keeping for later needs
senses.definition: described of a thing worth having because it will serve a need later
senses.definitionCN: 形容某物值得留着，因为日后会用得上
senses.example: Keep the box; it may come in useful when we move.
senses.exampleCN: 把箱子留着吧，搬家时也许用得上。
senses.why: A thing that can be put to work at any moment is worth keeping, and that practical judgement gives this sense.
senses.whyCN: 随时能拿来干活的东西自然值得保留，这层「留着有用」的实用判断由此产生。

senses.title: Producing good effects on people
senses.definition: having a good effect on a person's knowledge, health, or work
senses.definitionCN: 对某人的知识、健康或工作产生良好作用
senses.example: The trip was useful for her spoken English.
senses.exampleCN: 这趟旅行对她的口语很有帮助。
senses.why: From tools the word extends to anything that leaves a person better off, such as a lesson or a habit.
senses.whyCN: 从器物再往外延伸，凡是让人变得更好的东西（如一堂课、一个习惯）也可以这样形容。

senses.title: Practical rather than beautiful
senses.definition: plain and practical in design rather than attractive
senses.definitionCN: 设计朴素实用而不追求好看
senses.example: The kitchen is small but useful, with everything within reach.
senses.exampleCN: 厨房不大却很实用，东西伸手就能够到。
senses.why: If a thing is judged by how well it works, plainness stops being a fault; this sense praises function over looks.
senses.whyCN: 既然以「好不好使」来评判，朴素就不算缺点；这层义项正是对功能的称赞。

intro.en: A native suffix, full of, laid over the borrowed verb use; the compound has been in English since the Middle Ages.
intro.cn: 一个本土后缀「充满」压在借入的动词 use 之上，这个复合词在中古英语时期就已存在。

items.en: The suffix -full meant full or complete and was freely added to nouns.
items.cn: 后缀 -full 意为「满的、完全的」，可自由加在名词之后。

items.en: The base goes back to uti and its participle usus, a using.
items.cn: 词基可溯至 uti 及其分词 usus，意为「使用」。

items.en: Us and user carried the verb into French and from there into English.
items.cn: us 与 user 把这个动词带进法语，再进入英语。

items.en: Use and the suffix -ful combine, and the final l is later dropped in spelling.
items.cn: use 与后缀 -ful 结合，后来拼写中省去了末尾的一个 l。

items.en: Useful settles into the standard form, and usefully and usefulness follow it.
items.cn: useful 固定为标准写法，usefully 与 usefulness 相继派生。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words on the same use stem, and the near-meaning group sorts helpful words by strength.
note.cn: 形近组汇集同一 use 词干上的词，近义组按程度给「有帮助」一类的词排序。

entries.definition: to employ something for a purpose

normalIntro.en: Read it as use plus full: full of use, therefore worth having at hand.
normalIntro.cn: 把它读成 use 加 full：充满用处，因此值得随手带着。

normal.en: Use plus -ful follows the same pattern as helpful and careful.
normal.cn: use 加 -ful 与 helpful、careful 走的是同一构词路子。

normal.en: Come in useful is the idiom for something that turns out handy later.
normal.cn: come in useful 是「后来派上用场」的惯用说法。

normal.en: The negative partner is useless, with -less instead of -ful.
normal.cn: 否定形式是 useless，用的是 -less 而不是 -ful。

normal.en: Usefulness and usefully show the noun and adverb built on the same stem.
normal.cn: usefulness 与 usefully 是同词干上的名词和副词。

normal.en: In British spelling the word has one l before the end.
normal.cn: 英式拼写里这个词中间只有一个 l。

abstract.en: Picture a pocket knife that opens boxes, peels fruit, and cuts string.
abstract.cn: 想象一把小折刀，开箱、削果、割绳样样能干。

abstract.en: Hear a stranger say that your note saved them an afternoon.
abstract.cn: 听陌生人说，你那页笔记替他们省了一个下午。

abstract.en: Feel a torch click on in a sudden blackout.
abstract.cn: 体会突然停电时手电筒咔哒一声亮起。

examples.en: The leaflet gives useful advice on saving water at home.
examples.cn: 这份传单给了在家节水的有用建议。

examples.en: A folding chair is useful when guests arrive suddenly.
examples.cn: 客人突然来时折叠椅就派得上用场。

examples.en: He found the grammar notes useful before the exam.
examples.cn: 考试前他觉得那些语法笔记很有用。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「优思否」——一样东西好不好用，先想一想它能不能替你省力。

root: 本土后缀 -ful（充满）加动词 use（源自拉丁语 uti / usus，经古法语 user），整体义为「充满用处」

sensesIntro.en: A core of full of use splits into practical help, keeping for later, good effects on people, and plain functional design.
sensesIntro.cn: 「充满用处」这个核心分成四路：实际帮助、留着备用、对人有益、朴素实用。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pocket knife that answers many needs.
core.cn: 核心意象：一把能应付多种需要的小折刀。

branches.en: The task branch: it helps the job get done.
branches.cn: 任务分支：它帮着把事情办成。

branches.en: The keeping branch: it earns a place in the drawer.
branches.cn: 留存分支：它值得占住抽屉的一角。

branches.en: The person branch: someone is better off after it.
branches.cn: 对人的分支：有了它，人变得更好。

branches.en: The design branch: plain looks judged by how well it works.
branches.cn: 设计分支：朴素的外表以好不好使来评判。

branches.en: The judgement branch: worth is measured by future help.
branches.cn: 评判分支：价值按它日后能帮多少来衡量。

intro.en: A Germanic adjective suffix on a borrowed verb: what is full of use is useful.
intro.cn: 日耳曼语形容词后缀加在借入的动词上：充满用处的，就是有用的。

latinIntro.en: The stem comes from Latin uti, to use, whose participle usus gave the noun use.
latinIntro.cn: 词干来自拉丁语 uti（使用），其分词 usus 给出名词 use。

items.example: Use the small spoon for sugar.

items.exampleCN: usefully 说明有帮助地做事。
usefulness 命名这种性质本身。

items.example: A user is one who uses.
Usage records how something is used.
A misuse is a wrong use.

definition_zh: 用户；使用者；服用者
definition_en: a person or thing that uses something, especially a person who uses a service or product
core_image: 一个人低头在手机上一步步按着界面操作
scene: 图书馆新装的借书机前，年轻人排队试着操作，工作人员在一旁教第一次来的读者。Every new user needs a minute to learn the screen.
sceneCN: 这里 user 是「使用者、用户」（第 1 个义项：使用某物或某项服务的人）；句意为每个新用户都需要一点时间熟悉这块屏幕。低头操作界面的画面，正是这个词的核心。

derivatives.zh: 去掉后缀后的动词，义为「使用」
同族名词，义为「用法；使用量」
复合形容词，义为「易于使用的」
加 -able 的同族形容词，义为「可用的」

senses.title: A person who uses a product or service
senses.definition: someone who uses a product, service, or system, especially regularly
senses.definitionCN: 使用某产品、服务或系统的人，尤指经常使用的人
senses.example: The website asks every user to choose a password.
senses.exampleCN: 网站要求每位用户设置一个密码。
senses.why: The verb names the act of putting something to work; adding the agent suffix marks the person doing it.
senses.whyCN: 动词指「让东西干活」，加上表人的后缀，就指做这件事的那个人。

senses.title: Someone who takes drugs
senses.definition: a person who takes a drug, often habitually
senses.definitionCN: 服用药物的人，常指长期吸食毒品者
senses.example: The clinic helps long-term drug users rebuild their lives.
senses.exampleCN: 这家诊所帮助长期吸毒的人重建生活。
senses.why: A drug is also something taken into the body, so the same word carries over to the person who takes it.
senses.whyCN: 药物同样是进入身体的东西，于是这个词也延伸到了服用它的人身上。

senses.title: A device or person consuming a resource
senses.definition: a person or organisation that consumes water, power, or another supply
senses.definitionCN: 消耗水、电或其他资源的个人或机构
senses.example: The village is the largest water user in the valley.
senses.exampleCN: 这个村子是山谷里用水最多的一方。
senses.why: Since use also means spending a supply, an agent noun can describe whoever draws on that supply.
senses.whyCN: 既然 use 还有「耗用」之义，表人的名词自然也能指取用这份资源的那一方。

senses.title: A person skilled in handling something
senses.definition: a person who knows how to handle a tool or a situation well
senses.definitionCN: 懂得把工具或局面用得熟练的人
senses.example: He is a skilful user of words, able to calm any room.
senses.exampleCN: 他很会用词，能让任何场合安静下来。
senses.why: The same agent noun can praise skill, because the one who uses a thing well is the one who masters it.
senses.whyCN: 同一个表人名词也能表示赞赏：把东西用得好的人，就是掌握它的人。

intro.en: The agent suffix -er, native to English, added to the borrowed verb use.
intro.cn: 英语本土的表人后缀 -er 加在借入动词 use 之上。

items.en: The suffix -ere made agent nouns, as in writer and baker, and is still fully productive.
items.cn: 后缀 -ere 构成表人名词，如 writer、baker，至今仍能自由造词。

items.en: The base comes from uti, to use, with its participle usus.
items.cn: 词基来自 uti（使用）及其分词 usus。

items.en: The verb reached English through French as user, to use.
items.cn: 这个动词经法语 user（使用）进入英语。

items.en: User appears early for anyone who uses a thing, with no link to machines.
items.cn: user 早期泛指使用某物的人，与机器无关。

items.en: With computers and the internet the word becomes the standard term for the person at the screen.
items.cn: 随着电脑与互联网的普及，这个词成为指屏幕前那个人的标准说法。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the use family, and the near-meaning group names people in terms of what they consume or control.
note.cn: 形近组汇集 use 词族，近义组则从消耗或掌控的角度来称呼人。

entries.definition: a person who buys and uses goods
a person who buys from a shop
a person who works a machine
a person or firm that supplies a service

normalIntro.en: A plain agent noun: the one who uses is the user, exactly as a writer writes.
normalIntro.cn: 一个朴素的表人名词：谁是用的那个人，谁就是 user，正如写的人叫 writer。

normal.en: User follows the writer and baker pattern of verb plus -er.
normal.cn: user 走的是 writer、baker 那样「动词加 -er」的路子。

normal.en: User name and password are fixed pairs in every login box.
normal.cn: user name 与 password 是每个登录框里的固定搭配。

normal.en: Heavy user suggests a habit, while first-time user suggests novelty.
normal.cn: heavy user 暗示习惯，first-time user 暗示初次接触。

normal.en: The adjective is user-friendly, a modern compound.
normal.cn: 形容词形式是 user-friendly，属于现代复合词。

normal.en: Drug user is a medical or social term, not a technical one.
normal.cn: drug user 是医学或社会用语，并非技术术语。

abstract.en: Picture a queue at a self-service machine, each person learning the screen.
abstract.cn: 想象自助机前排着队，每个人都在学怎么用那块屏幕。

abstract.en: Hear the click of a login page opening on a phone.
abstract.cn: 听手机上一声轻响，登录页弹出。

abstract.en: See worn spots on a keyboard where the same fingers always land.
abstract.cn: 看键盘上被同一副手指磨出来的那几处。

examples.en: Each user of the shared bike must lock it afterwards.
examples.cn: 每位共享单车用户都必须之后锁好车。

examples.en: The guide was written for users with no technical training.
examples.cn: 这本指南是写给没有技术背景的使用者的。

examples.en: A heavy user of electricity will notice the bill at once.
examples.cn: 用电大户立刻就能感到账单的变化。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「优择」——挑来挑去，最后选中使用的就是用户。

root: 本土表人后缀 -er 加动词 use（拉丁语 uti / usus，经古法语 user），义为「使用的人」

sensesIntro.en: One agent noun branches from using products to taking drugs, from drawing on a supply to mastering a skill.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个表人名词，从使用产品分到吸食药物，从耗用资源分到精于此道。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person at a screen, learning how it works.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人面对着屏幕，熟悉它的用法。

branches.en: The product branch: the person a service is built for.
branches.cn: 产品分支：服务所围绕的那个人。

branches.en: The drug branch: the body as the thing being used.
branches.cn: 药物分支：身体成了被使用的对象。

branches.en: The resource branch: whoever draws water or power.
branches.cn: 资源分支：取水取电的那一方。

branches.en: The skill branch: skill turns a user into a master.
branches.cn: 技艺分支：熟练使使用者变成行家。

branches.en: The consumption branch: using always takes something up.
branches.cn: 消耗分支：凡是使用总要占用掉一些什么。

intro.en: A verb plus the native agent suffix: the person who performs the action.
intro.cn: 动词加本土表人后缀：执行这个动作的人。

latinIntro.en: The base is Latin uti and its participle usus; the suffix -er is Germanic, not Latin.
latinIntro.cn: 词基是拉丁语 uti 及其分词 usus；-er 后缀是日耳曼语成分，不是拉丁语。

items.example: Use both hands on the wheel.
A user is one who uses.
Usage is the way of using.
Useful is built on the same base.
items.exampleCN: useful 也建在同一词基上。

items.example: Usable means able to be used.
A writer is the matching agent noun.
items.exampleCN: writer 是同构的表人名词。

items.example: A baker shows -er at work again.
items.exampleCN: baker 再次显示 -er 的作用。

definition_zh: 通常的；平常的；一贯的；惯常的
definition_en: happening or done most of the time, and therefore normal for a person or place
core_image: 每天早上七点同一个座位上一杯同样的咖啡
scene: 清晨的小店刚开门，靠窗那张桌子已经坐上了熟客，点的还是那杯不加水的美式。He sat at his usual table and ordered the same coffee.
sceneCN: 这里 usual 是「通常的、惯常的」（第 1 个义项：多数时候都如此）；句意为老顾客坐着他常坐的那张桌子，喝着常点的咖啡。每天早上同一杯咖啡的画面，正是这个词的核心。

derivatives.zh: 加 -ly 构成副词，义为「通常；一般」
加否定前缀 un-，义为「不寻常的」
同根动词，义为「使用」
同根名词，义为「用法；惯例」

senses.title: What normally happens
senses.definition: describing what happens most often or is most often seen
senses.definitionCN: 形容最常发生或最常见的情况
senses.example: The usual bus is ten minutes late in the rain.
senses.exampleCN: 下雨时那班常坐的公交总会晚十分钟。
senses.why: The Latin source names what custom has made habitual, and habit is simply what happens most of the time.
senses.whyCN: 这个词的拉丁来源指「习俗使之成为常态的东西」，而习惯也就是大多数时候都会发生的事。

senses.title: Customary for one person or place
senses.definition: describing a fixed habit of one particular person, family, or shop
senses.definitionCN: 形容某个人、家庭或店铺固定不变的习惯
senses.example: She took her usual walk along the river after dinner.
senses.exampleCN: 晚饭后她照例沿着河走一走。
senses.why: Custom is personal as well as general, so the word also marks the private routines that repeat every day.
senses.whyCN: 习俗既属于众人也属于个人，所以这个词也用来标记每天重复的私人习惯。

senses.title: The ordinary option in a shop
senses.definition: in informal speech, the food or drink one always orders
senses.definitionCN: 口语中指某人每次固定点的那份饮食
senses.example: The waiter brought him the usual without asking.
senses.exampleCN: 服务员问都没问就给他端来了老样子。
senses.why: Once a choice is repeated often enough, it becomes a name in itself, and people simply order the usual.
senses.whyCN: 一个选择重复得够多就成了它自己的名字，人们于是干脆说「老样子」。

senses.title: That is as expected, nothing new
senses.definition: used of an unpleasant event that is exactly what one would expect
senses.definitionCN: 用于形容某件不愉快的事完全在意料之中
senses.example: His usual excuse was that the train was late again.
senses.exampleCN: 他还是那套老借口：火车又晚点了。
senses.why: Because habitual things are predictable, the word easily carries a faint tone of weary expectation.
senses.whyCN: 惯常之事总是可预料的，于是这个词也容易带上一丝厌烦的「又是这样」的意味。

intro.en: From Latin through French: a word about custom and habit, whose base is shared with use.
intro.cn: 经由法语来自拉丁语：一个关于习俗与习惯的词，其词基与 use 同源。

items.en: Usus meant use, practice, and custom; usualis described what custom made ordinary.
items.cn: usus 意为使用、实践与习俗；usualis 形容习俗使之成为常态的事物。

items.en: The form usualis is recorded as an adjective of everyday practice.
items.cn: usualis 这一形式有记录，用作指日常实践的形容词。

items.en: Usuel and the learned usual entered French usage alongside the everyday us.
items.cn: usuel 与书面形式 usual 同日常的 us 一起在法语中并行。

items.en: Usual enters English in the fourteenth century, first in legal and church writing.
items.cn: usual 于十四世纪进入英语，最早见于法律与教会文书。

items.en: The everyday phrases as usual and business as usual make the word home in ordinary speech.
items.cn: as usual 与 business as usual 这些日常说法让这个词彻底扎根于口语。

note.en: The look-alike group shows the use family behind usual, and the near-meaning group gathers words for what is normal.
note.cn: 形近组展示 usual 背后的 use 词族，近义组汇集表示「正常」的一类词。

normalIntro.en: Think of custom turned into an adjective: what a person or place always does.
normalIntro.cn: 把「习俗」变成形容词来想：某个人或某个地方总是这么做。

normal.en: As usual is a two-word phrase meaning in the normal way.
normal.cn: as usual 是两个词组成的短语，意为「像平常一样」。

normal.en: Business as usual says that nothing has changed.
normal.cn: business as usual 表示一切照旧。

normal.en: The adverb usually is far more frequent in speech than the adjective.
normal.cn: 副词 usually 在口语中比形容词本身常用得多。

normal.en: Unusual is the common opposite, formed with un-.
normal.cn: unusual 是用 un- 构成的常见反义词。

normal.en: Usual shares its root with use and usage.
normal.cn: usual 与 use、usage 同根。

abstract.en: Picture the same window seat taken every morning at seven.
abstract.cn: 想象每天早上七点都占着同一个靠窗座位。

abstract.en: Hear a waiter say the usual before you sit down.
abstract.cn: 听服务员在你落座前就说「老样子」。

abstract.en: Notice a worn path across the grass where everyone walks.
abstract.cn: 留意草地上被大家踩出来的一条小径。

examples.en: As usual, she arrived ten minutes before the meeting began.
examples.cn: 像往常一样，她在会议开始前十分钟就到了。

examples.en: He ordered his usual soup and read the paper.
examples.cn: 他点了常喝的那份汤，看着报纸。

examples.en: The shop keeps its usual hours even during the holiday.
examples.cn: 假期里这家店也保持着平常的营业时间。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「优若」——习惯的事做起来总是优若自然，不必多想。

root: 拉丁语 usus（使用、实践、习俗）派生 usualis，经古法语 usuel / usual 进入英语，义为「按习俗常行的」

sensesIntro.en: From custom comes what happens most of the time, then personal routines, then the fixed order, and finally the weary expected excuse.
sensesIntro.cn: 从习俗出发，先指多数时候发生的事，再指个人日常、固定点单，最后是那句听腻了的预料之中的借口。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the same seat and the same coffee every morning.
core.cn: 核心意象：每天早上同一张座位、同一杯咖啡。

branches.en: The habit branch: what happens on most days.
branches.cn: 习惯分支：大多数日子都会发生的事。

branches.en: The person branch: this family or shop always does so.
branches.cn: 个体分支：这一家、这一店总是如此。

branches.en: The order branch: the dish repeated until it has a name.
branches.cn: 点单分支：重复到有了名字的那份菜。

branches.en: The excuse branch: expected, and therefore tiring.
branches.cn: 借口分支：全然预料之中，因此令人厌倦。

branches.en: The expectation branch: habit makes events predictable.
branches.cn: 预期分支：习惯让事情变得可以预测。

intro.en: An adjective ending on a stem shared with use, formed in Latin and polished in French.
intro.cn: 一个形容词，接在与 use 同源的词干上，成形于拉丁语，经法语打磨。

latinIntro.en: Latin usus, use and custom, yields the adjective usualis, whose ending -alis becomes English -al.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 usus（使用与习俗）派生出形容词 usualis，其词尾 -alis 变成英语的 -al。

items.example: The stem us- carries the idea of custom.
items.exampleCN: 词干 us- 承载「习俗」之义。

items.example: Usually marks what happens in the normal way.
items.exampleCN: usually 标记按常规发生的事。

items.example: Usualness is rarely needed in speech.
items.exampleCN: usualness 在口语中很少用到。

items.example: Use and usual share one root.

items.exampleCN: usage 记录习俗所认可的说法。

items.example: Custom is the plain English partner.
items.exampleCN: custom 是这个词朴素的英语伙伴。

definition_zh: 通常；经常；一般；照例
definition_en: in most cases, or on most occasions
core_image: 一年里绝大多数早晨，同一扇窗在同一个时刻亮起
scene: 邻居家那盏厨房灯总是六点半准时亮起，只有停电那天例外。She usually leaves for work before the streets get busy.
sceneCN: 这里 usually 是「通常、一般」（第 1 个义项：多数情况下如此）；句意为她一般在街上还没忙起来时就出门上班。每天同一时刻亮起的厨房灯，正是这个词的核心。

derivatives.zh: 去掉 -ly 后的形容词，义为「通常的；平常的」
加否定前缀 un-，义为「不寻常地」
同根动词，义为「使用」
同根名词，义为「用法；惯例」

senses.title: In most cases
senses.definition: used to say what happens in the majority of situations
senses.definitionCN: 用来说明在大多数情形下会发生什么
senses.example: Trains here usually run on time.
senses.exampleCN: 这里的火车通常准点运行。
senses.why: The adjective names what custom makes normal; the adverb turns that frequency into a statement about how often things happen.
senses.whyCN: 形容词指习俗使之成为常态的东西，加 -ly 成副词后，就把这种「常态」变成对发生频率的说明。

senses.title: As a settled habit
senses.definition: used of a person's regular practice rather than of things in general
senses.definitionCN: 用于说明某个人一贯的做法，而不是泛指一般情况
senses.example: He usually walks to the office unless it rains.
senses.exampleCN: 除非下雨，他通常走着去办公室。
senses.why: Habits are personal customs, so the adverb also marks what a particular person always does.
senses.whyCN: 习惯属于个人的习俗，因此这个副词也用来标记某个人一贯的做法。

senses.title: Generally true, with exceptions
senses.definition: weakening a general statement so that exceptions are allowed
senses.definitionCN: 用来弱化一个概括说法，为例外留出余地
senses.example: Books like this are usually written for beginners.
senses.exampleCN: 这类书一般是写给初学者的。
senses.why: Because custom holds most of the time rather than always, the adverb naturally signals a rule with exceptions.
senses.whyCN: 习俗只是多数时候成立而非绝对，所以这个副词天然带上「大体如此、但有例外」的语气。

senses.title: In the normal place or condition
senses.definition: used to state where or in what state something is normally found
senses.definitionCN: 用于说明某物通常出现在何处或以何种状态存在
senses.example: The keys are usually in the drawer by the door.
senses.exampleCN: 钥匙一般在门边的抽屉里。
senses.why: A fixed routine creates a fixed place for things, so the adverb also answers the everyday question of where something normally is.
senses.whyCN: 固定的习惯会为东西定下固定的位置，于是这个副词也用来回答「东西一般放在哪儿」。

intro.en: The adverb formed from usual with the native suffix -ly; behind it lies Latin usus, custom.
intro.cn: 由 usual 加本土副词后缀 -ly 构成，背后是拉丁语 usus（习俗）。

items.en: Usus meant use, practice, and custom, and usualis described what custom made ordinary.
items.cn: usus 意为使用、实践与习俗，usualis 形容习俗使之成为常态的事物。

items.en: Usuel carried the adjective into French, where adverbs were already regularly made with a -ment or -ment/-ly pattern.
items.cn: usuel 把形容词带进法语，当时的副词已有固定的构成方式。

items.en: The adjective usual arrives in the fourteenth century and the adverb usually follows in the fifteenth.
items.cn: 形容词 usual 于十四世纪进入英语，副词 usually 于十五世纪随后出现。

items.en: Usually grows into one of the most frequent sentence adverbs in written and spoken English.
items.cn: usually 逐渐成为书面与口语中最常见的句子副词之一。

items.en: Newspaper style prefers usually to the longer phrase in most cases.
items.cn: 报刊文体更爱用 usually，而不写较长的 in most cases。

note.en: The look-alike group is the usual family with its suffixes, and the near-meaning group ranks frequency adverbs.
note.cn: 形近组是 usual 词族及其后缀形式，近义组把表示频率的副词按高低排开。

entries.definition: in a way that is not normal
in a relaxed way, only the spelling looks close, the root is different
entries.definitionCN: 随意地；只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: in most cases, on the whole

normalIntro.en: Take the adjective of custom and add the plain adverb ending; what is usual happens usually.
normalIntro.cn: 把表示习俗的形容词加上最普通的副词词尾：usual 的事就 usually 发生。

normal.en: Usually sits mid-sentence, before the main verb: usually runs, usually walks.
normal.cn: usually 常位于句中主要动词之前，如 usually runs、usually walks。

normal.en: The negative partner is unusually, not rarely.
normal.cn: 它的否定形式是 unusually，而不是 rarely。

normal.en: Usually before a general subject talks about things, not people.
normal.cn: usually 与泛指主语连用时说的是事物，不是某个人。

normal.en: In formal writing the phrases tend to and as a rule compete with it.
normal.cn: 正式写作里 tend to 与 as a rule 与它竞争。

normal.en: Usual and usually share one stem with use and usage.
normal.cn: usual 与 usually 跟 use、usage 共用一个词干。

abstract.en: Picture a kitchen window lighting up at half past six every morning.
abstract.cn: 想象每天早上六点半亮起的那扇厨房窗。

abstract.en: Hear the same train announced on the same platform.
abstract.cn: 听同一站台反复播报同一趟车。

abstract.en: Notice the one day the shop shuts early, and remember it as the exception.
abstract.cn: 留意商店唯一一次提前关门，把它当作例外记住。

examples.en: I usually take the side road when the main street is jammed.
examples.cn: 主街堵车时我通常走小路。

examples.en: These birds are usually seen near water in winter.
examples.cn: 这些鸟冬天一般在近水处出现。

examples.en: She usually finishes her report before Friday.
examples.cn: 她一般在周五前就把报告写完。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「优若利」——习惯的事做起来总是优若顺利，不必费力。

root: 形容词 usual（拉丁语 usus / usualis，经古法语）加副词后缀 -ly，义为「按惯例地、通常」

sensesIntro.en: From custom in general the adverb moves to personal habit, to a rule with exceptions, and to the normal place of things.
sensesIntro.cn: 从一般的习俗出发，这个副词先指个人习惯，再指有例外的通则，最后指事物常处的位置。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one window lighting up at the same minute all year.
core.cn: 核心意象：一整年里同一分钟亮起的一扇窗。

branches.en: The frequency branch: this is what happens on most days.
branches.cn: 频率分支：大多数日子都是这样。

branches.en: The habit branch: one person's regular practice.
branches.cn: 习惯分支：某个人一贯的做法。

branches.en: The exception branch: a general truth that allows cases against it.
branches.cn: 例外分支：允许反面情况的概括之论。

branches.en: The place branch: the spot where things are normally found.
branches.cn: 位置分支：东西平常所在之处。

branches.en: The expectation branch: prediction with a margin of doubt.
branches.cn: 预期分支：留有疑问余地的预测。

intro.en: The most ordinary adverb ending in English laid on an adjective of custom.
intro.cn: 英语里最普通的副词词尾，加在一个表示习俗的形容词上。

latinIntro.en: The stem is Latin usus, custom and practice, with the adjective ending -alis becoming -al.
latinIntro.cn: 词干是拉丁语 usus（习俗、实践），形容词词尾 -alis 变成 -al。

items.example: The stem points to settled practice.
items.exampleCN: 词干指向固定下来的做法。

items.example: Usually says in the customary way.
items.exampleCN: usually 表示按惯例的方式。

items.example: Use belongs to the same family.
Usage records what people usually say.
items.exampleCN: usage 记录人们通常怎么说。

items.example: Normally is a close rival adverb.
items.exampleCN: normally 是相近的竞争副词。

items.example: In most cases means much the same.
items.exampleCN: in most cases 意思相仿。

definition_zh: 假期；度假；休庭期
definition_en: a period of time away from work or school, often spent travelling
core_image: 行李箱敞在床上，一半是泳衣一半是防晒霜
scene: 七月的最后一天，办公室的灯一盏盏关掉，同事把文件夹压在桌上，说下周谁也不许找他。They spent their vacation on a quiet island.
sceneCN: 这里 vacation 是「假期」（第 1 个义项：离开工作或学习的休假期）；句意为他们在一个安静的小岛上度假。敞开的行李箱，正是这个词的核心。

derivatives.zh: 同根动词，义为「腾出；空出」
同根形容词，义为「空的；空缺的」
同根名词，义为「空缺；空房」
加 -er 构成，义为「度假者」

senses.title: Time away from work or school
senses.definition: a period of some days or weeks when work or school stops
senses.definitionCN: 工作或学习停顿的一段天数或周数
senses.example: They took a three-week vacation in the mountains.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在山里休了三周假。
senses.why: The Latin noun first named a being free of duties, so the holiday is simply the period when those duties are lifted.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁名词最初指「免除职责」这一状态，所以假期就是职责被撤下的那段时间。

senses.title: A trip taken during such time
senses.definition: used of travelling or resting away from home during a holiday
senses.definitionCN: 指在假期里离家旅行或休息
senses.example: The whole family spent the vacation by the sea.
senses.exampleCN: 一家人整个假期都待在海边。
senses.why: Once the days are free, the journey that fills them takes the same name, and the trip becomes the vacation.
senses.whyCN: 日子一旦空出来，填满它的旅程也取了同样的名字，旅行本身就成了 vacation。

senses.title: A break granted by a court or office
senses.definition: a fixed break for a court or an institution
senses.definitionCN: 法院或机构固定的休止期
senses.example: The court is in vacation until early September.
senses.exampleCN: 法院休庭到九月初。
senses.why: Institutions also empty out for fixed weeks, so law keeps the word for the bench left sitting idle.
senses.whyCN: 机构也会在固定的几周里空下来，法律便用这个词指闲着的法官席。

senses.title: The act of giving up a post
senses.definition: in older use, the act of vacating a position or a place
senses.definitionCN: 旧时用法，指辞去或腾出一个职位、一处场所
senses.example: His vacation of the chair left the office empty for a year.
senses.exampleCN: 他辞去这一席位，让该职位空了一年。
senses.why: This is the oldest legal sense: the act of making a place empty by leaving it.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的法律义：离开一处场所，从而使它空出来。

intro.en: A Latin noun of exemption from duty, whose root also gives vacant and vacuum.
intro.cn: 一个表示「免除职责」的拉丁名词，其词根也给出 vacant 与 vacuum。

items.en: Vacare meant to be free of duty, and vacatio named the state of being exempt.
items.cn: vacare 意为「免于职责」，vacatio 指处于免除状态。

items.en: In legal use vacatio covered the free days of courts, when no case was heard.
items.cn: 在法律用语中，vacatio 指法院不审案的空闲日子。

items.en: Vacation carried the legal and ecclesiastical sense into French.
items.cn: vacation 把法律与教会的这层含义带进法语。

items.en: English borrows the word in the fourteenth century, first for the law courts and the universities.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪借入这个词，最初用于法院与大学。

items.en: From the nineteenth century the word names the ordinary holiday of any worker.
items.cn: 自十九世纪起，这个词泛指任何工作者的普通假期。

note.en: The look-alike group shows the vac- family of freedom and emptiness, and the near-meaning group places rest beside work.
note.cn: 形近组展示表示「空、自由」的 vac- 词族，近义组把休息与工作相对照。

entries.definition: a calling to a kind of work, only the ending is close, the root is different
entries.definitionCN: 职业；只是词尾相近，词源不同

entries.definition: the working part of a school year

normalIntro.en: A vacation is literally an emptying of the calendar: the days are cleared and left free.
normalIntro.cn: vacation 字面上就是把日历腾空：日子被清出来，空着。

normal.en: Go on vacation and take a vacation are the two set phrases.
normal.cn: go on vacation 与 take a vacation 是两个固定说法。

normal.en: American English says vacation where British English says holiday.
normal.cn: 美式说 vacation，英式说 holiday。

normal.en: The legal sense survives in court in vacation.
normal.cn: 法律义仍留在 court in vacation 这样的说法里。

normal.en: The root vac- links vacation to vacant and vacancy.
normal.cn: 词根 vac- 把 vacation 与 vacant、vacancy 连起来。

normal.en: Vacationer is mainly American and means a traveller on holiday.
normal.cn: vacationer 主要是美式用法，指度假的游客。

abstract.en: Picture a suitcase half packed at the foot of a bed.
abstract.cn: 想象床脚一只装了一半的箱子。

abstract.en: See a desk calendar with two empty weeks crossed out in yellow.
abstract.cn: 看台历上被黄色涂掉的两个空周。

abstract.en: Hear the click of office lights going off one by one.
abstract.cn: 听办公室的灯一盏盏关掉的声音。

examples.en: We spent our vacation walking in the hills.
examples.cn: 我们假期在山里徒步。

examples.en: She booked two weeks of vacation in August.
examples.cn: 她订了八月两周的休假。

examples.en: The court will sit again after the long vacation.
examples.cn: 法院在长休庭期之后会再次开庭。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「我会开心」——假期一到，我就会开心。

root: 拉丁语 vacare（空着、免于职责）→ vacatio（免除职务、空闲），经古法语 vacation 进入英语

sensesIntro.en: An emptying of duty becomes the free time, then the trip taken in it, then an institution's pause, and in old law a post given up.
sensesIntro.cn: 把职责腾空，先成空出的时间，再成填满它的旅行，再成机构的停歇，旧法里还指让出的职位。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a suitcase half packed on a bed.
core.cn: 核心意象：床上一只装了一半的行李箱。
